s.t: Jack Antonoff gave each of its three verses to a different person in his family: “First verse is me, second is my father, third is my mother.”
s.src: BuzzFeed: Jack Antonoff interview on Take the Sadness Out of Saturday Night
s.q: First verse is me, second is my father, third is my mother.

s.t: Jack Antonoff said the title is a literal voice inside him, rooted in the Eastern European Jewish fear of tempting the evil eye by wanting too good a life.
s.src: Rolling Stone: Jack Antonoff Is Everywhere (Brian Hiatt, 2021)
s.q: It's like, 'Be careful, don't tempt the evil eye. Don't try to have too good a life.' ... there's a literal voice in me, which is the 'how dare you want more' voice. The idea of tempting the evil eye is a real Eastern European Jewish thing.

s.t: Jack Antonoff called this recording “the band on fire”, saying no other group could have made it after so long on the road learning what each other would do.
s.src: The Line of Best Fit: Bleachers release new track How Dare You Want More
s.q: This one is the band on fire. Testing the boundaries of how close we can get to the edge without falling off. This recording could not have happened with any other group of people and its the direct sound of all the time we’ve spent on the road and how we’ve learned to know what each other is going to do.

s.t: Bleachers played it on their last-minute Saturday Night Live debut in January 2022, standing in for Roddy Ricch, with Jack Antonoff’s father, Rick Antonoff, on guitar.
s.src: Stereogum: Watch Bleachers Make Their Saturday Night Live Debut
s.q: stepped in at the last-minute to make its debut on the show ... brought along his dad Rick to play guitar ... Roddy Ricch was the planned musical guest

f.t: In 2017 Jack Antonoff packed the whole contents of his New Jersey bedroom, where he lived until he was 27, into a trailer that went on tour with the band.
f.src: Stereogum: Bleachers’ Jack Antonoff Is Taking His Childhood Bedroom On Tour
f.q: he’s extracted the entire contents of his bedroom from his childhood home in New Jersey ... packed it in a trailer, which will accompany Bleachers on tour ... although “childhood” is stretching it, because he lived there until age 27

f.t: In August 2026 NJ Transit temporarily renamed its North Jersey Coast Line the “Bleachers Coast Line” for their Shadow of the City festival at the Stone Pony in Asbury Park.
f.q: NJ TRANSIT is branding its North Jersey Coast Line rail service as “Bleachers Coast Line” to celebrate the band’s annual “Shadow of the City” Festival at the legendary Stone Pony in Asbury Park on August 28.

f.t: Jack Antonoff hears songs in a female voice as he writes, then sings them an octave lower to hit the notes; that’s why so many are sung so low.
f.src: Stereogum: Charli XCX, Carly Rae Jepsen, Sia and others cover Bleachers
f.q: when i write songs i typically hear things in a female voice and then match it an octave lower so i can hit the notes. that's why so many bleachers' songs are sung so low.

f.t: The name came out during a drive with Jack Antonoff’s sister, and was first the title of the song ‘Like a River Runs’; he called it “the coolest name”.
f.src: American Songwriter: The Dark Reality Behind the Band Name Bleachers
f.q: The word bleachers was the original title of “Like a River Runs” off Strange Desire which Antonoff called “the coolest name.” ... “I was driving with my sister and we were talking about the feelings and influences of the music and the word just like came out.

nf.t: Three verses, three people: Jack Antonoff, then his father, then his mother.
nf.src: BuzzFeed: Jack Antonoff interview on Take the Sadness Out of Saturday Night
nf.q: First verse is me, second is my father, third is my mother.
